lyric_idea: Verse 2: "And I can't even parallel park" is the speaker failing a small driving task while machines drive cars and walk themselves off factory lines. On-screen: a robotaxi stat, the driving-jobs-most-exposed line, a humanoid doing household chores, and a humanoid walking out of a production line by itself. No lyric text on screen.

candidates.text: 500,000 paid robotaxi rides every week across 10 U.S. cities (on-screen source line: Waymo, via TechCrunch, Mar 2026)
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Waymo, as reported by TechCrunch (Kirsten Korosec)
candidates.verified_how: Live: TechCrunch article opened. Headline "Waymo's skyrocketing ridership in one chart", byline Kirsten Korosec, Mar 27 2026 12:11 PM PDT. Sentence read from the page: "Waymo is now providing 500,000 paid robotaxi rides every week across 10 U.S. cities". Waymo's own blog index (opened, Oct 2026) states no ride count, so the figure rests on TechCrunch's report of Waymo's post. Deck: work/rev2/robotwork.json item robotwork-claude-rating-taxi-drivers repeats ~500k paid rides/week, which is Claude's own sourced figure in the data release and is not independently verified there. Caveat: March 2026 is the newest ride figure I could verify. Later single-source claims (14-15 cities, ~4,000 vehicles, another ~500k) were not confirmed and are not used. Tesla: live results were third-party trackers that disagree on which cities are unsupervised, with no Tesla primary source opened, so no Tesla candidate.
candidates.why_it_fits: The lyric is about failing to drive. A robotaxi stat is the most direct echo: a machine driving paying passengers at scale. Stat card reads in about 2 s.
